formNote: A counting sign: two parallel lines. Cosmological readings (Heaven and Earth) are later and interpretive.
summary: Two — the simplest written number, and in thought the sign of polarity and division. Negated as 不二 it names a non-duality that declines to split experience into subject and object, pure and impure, this and that.
placement: In the eye of the right wing, mirroring 不: two foci, one unbroken trajectory weaving around both.

readings.extraNote: Readings beyond Unihan’s list, added by Baracus from general knowledge; not yet checked.

satellites.title: The Dharma-Gate of Non-Duality
satellites.evidence: 不二 renders Sanskrit advaya, “not-two”. In chapter 9 of the Vimalakīrtinirdeśa, bodhisattvas discuss entry into non-duality; Mañjuśrī sets it beyond verbal explanation, and Vimalakīrti responds in silence.

checked.note: Chapter 9 ends with Mañjuśrī’s response and Vimalakīrti’s silence; this check establishes the Chinese passage, not the Sanskrit lexical correspondence.

satellites.title: Not-Two Is Not “One”
satellites.evidence: Buddhist advaya and Vedāntic advaita are both rendered “non-duality”, but their philosophical uses need context. Advaita Vedānta articulates non-duality through Brahman; Madhyamaka argues through dependent arising and emptiness. Neither label is a complete account of every school using it.
satellites.caveat: A comparison of philosophical uses, not an etymological contrast. The Sanskrit dictionary establishes lexical meanings; a detailed comparison of the traditions still needs specialist sources.
gaps: Specialist sources for the doctrinal comparison; the dictionary alone does not establish it.

satellites.title: The Pivot of the Way
satellites.evidence: “Where ‘that’ (彼) and ‘this’ (是) no longer find their opposite — this is called the pivot of the Way.” Zhuangzi’s critique of either-or disputation predates the arrival of Buddhism: an indigenous Chinese resonance with 不二.

checked.note: 彼是莫得其偶，謂之道樞

satellites.title: Without a Second
satellites.evidence: Malay tiada duanya means “peerless, without a second” — a structural echo of “not-two”, though it praises uniqueness rather than naming non-duality. French non-dualité is a modern scholarly term.
gaps: French usage of non-dualité is uncited.
